title: TypeScript SDK: conversion patterns between AsyncIterator and Web Streams with cancellation semantics and streaming-aware retries
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: Consumers of the TypeScript SDK use either AsyncIterator (for-for-await) or Web ReadableStream APIs. We need a well-documented, tested set of conversion helpers and runtime behaviors that preserve backpressure, propagate cancellations/errors, and allow streaming-aware retry policies without surprising double-delivery or deadlocks.

Goals:
- Provide two stable helper APIs: toReadableStream(asyncIterable) and toAsyncIterable(readableStream).
- Define and implement cancellation semantics: consumer .cancel()/return() should propagate to the underlying request, close the server-side KV/cache usage, and release batching tokens.
- Design streaming-aware retry contract: small transient errors (network hiccups, 5xx) should allow resumable retries where possible; non-resumable errors must surface and terminate the stream cleanly.
- Provide clear examples for common patterns (for-await with backpressure, piping to Response/next.js streaming, server-side streaming proxies).
- Avoid breaking changes to existing SDK consumers and keep ergonomics simple for usage with frameworks (Next.js, Deno, Cloudflare Workers where Streams are available).
acceptance_criteria: APIs exported: toReadableStream(asyncIterable) and toAsyncIterable(readableStream) with documented edge cases
Cancellation from consumer calls underlying request abort and releases resources (verified in unit tests)
Retry helper streamWithRetries(asyncIterableFactory, retryPolicy) that retries only at safe cut points and deduplicates partial items
Compatibility tests cover Node (native Web Streams), Deno, and a browser environment (lib.dom) using polyfills where needed
End-to-end example in docs demonstrating piping an LLM stream to fetch Response and to a Next.js streaming SSR endpoint
Performance regression <3% p50 on our microbench relative to baseline when using the helpers
Type definitions and JSDoc for all public helpers included
Design doc and API proposal reviewed and approved by SDK and API owners (links in comments)
implementation_notes: Core idea: treat the AsyncIterator as the canonical production runtime primitive and implement toReadableStream by pulling from iterator and enqueuing to a controller with proper backpressure handling.

Cancellation path: implement an AbortController per streaming request; wire iterator.return() to call underlying abort; make SDK's HTTP client accept an AbortSignal so network short-circuits happen immediately.

Retry policy: implement streamWithRetries that accepts a factory returning a fresh async iterator. Retry only when the failure happens between top-level items (we define item boundaries at newline-delimited JSON/chunk boundaries for streaming formats). For binary or opaque chunks, retry is disabled by default and must be opt-in with a user-provided reconstructor function.

Backpressure: when converting AsyncIterator -> ReadableStream, honor controller.desiredSize and pause pulling when desiredSize <= 0. In Node 18+ using built-in Web Streams this maps cleanly; in older Node use our internal polyfill shim to emulate desiredSize behavior.

Edge cases: when toAsyncIterable(readableStream) receives a stream that errors mid-chunk, we expose the error on iteration.next() and then ensure subsequent calls return done:true to avoid hanging iterators.

API ergonomics: keep helpers small and composable. Expose a low-level hook createStreamingSession(options) for internal use (not public) to avoid surface API churn. Public helpers will be thin wrappers.
Security: make sure AbortSignal propagation doesn't accidentally swallow audit events; keep audit/logging hooks invoked on cancel/error/complete paths.

Trade-offs: implementing resumable retries for arbitrary streaming protocols is complex — we will support resumable retries for newline-delimited-JSON (NDJSON) streams first, and require explicit opt-in for other formats. This keeps default semantics simple and avoids partial-delivery duplication.
Docs: include recipes for piping to Response, consuming with for-await, and implementing a streaming-to-file download with progress events. Include a small FAQ about double-delivery and idempotency.

Testing: add unit tests for controller.desiredSize pauses, cancellation propagation, retry rosaries, and cross-environment smoke tests using Playwright for browser flow. Add benchmark harness for microbench regression tests.

comments: 2026-02-26 - Ava Chen: Initial ticket created after spike. Spike notes attached in docs: https://drive.redwood/example/streaming-spike. TL;DR: two-way conversion works, but cancellation semantics need careful handling in older Node versions.

2026-03-02 - Diego Morales: Pushed initial branch feature/sdk/ENG-15321-convert-streams. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1482. The PR contains the first pass of toReadableStream and toAsyncIterable with unit tests for Node 18+.

2026-03-04 - Priya Nair (review): Left feedback on PR about desiredSize handling and a potential race when controller.close() races with enqueue() after iterator completes. Suggest adding an explicit draining flag.
2026-03-06 - Diego Morales: Addressed race by setting a draining boolean and converting enqueues to tryEnqueue wrapper; added tests that simulate slow consumer (desiredSize <= 0).
2026-03-08 - QA (Jon Patel): Found a failing case in Deno where ReadableStream.readableLock is different; added environment detection and fallback to a simple queue if native controller unavailable.

2026-03-10 - Diego Morales: Implemented streamWithRetries skeleton. Current behavior: retries only for NDJSON streams where last emitted token ended with '
'. We also dedupe partially-processed buffered chunk state by using a reconstructor that resets at item boundaries.
2026-03-11 - Documentation (Marta Silva): Drafted examples for Next.js and Cloudflare Worker. Link: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/streaming-interop. Need a short idiomatic example for new users.

2026-03-12 - Diego Morales: Running benchmarks. Preliminary results: p50 latency regression ~1.8% when converting through helpers vs direct iterator consumption (acceptable). Preparing final PR updates and CHANGES entry.
2026-03-12 - PM (Rohit Gupta): Approved scope for 2.4.0 if tests pass and perf is within budget. Please coordinate release notes and include migration notes for any deprecated patterns.
